title: Calendar Afternoon Fragmentation
app: Obsidian Sync, Todoist, Toggl Track, Google Calendar / iCloud calendar exports, and task metadata ingested into Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:freebusy
| eval hour=tonumber(strftime(_time,"%H"))
| where hour>=13 AND hour<18
| bin _time span=1d
| stats dc(slot_start) as busy_blocks, sum(busy_min) as busy_min by _time
| where busy_blocks>5 AND busy_min>180
| sort - busy_blocks
description: Uses Calendar free-busy blocks telemetry to monitor how fragmented afternoon time becomes in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for days where deep work is unlikely because the afternoon is chopped up, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Calendar free-busy blocks data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a daily cadence.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Digital Life & Productivity — typical feeds: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), Apple/Android screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar/todo exports..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `calendar:freebusy`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=calendar:freebusy`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, and calendar feeds via HEC scripted inputs..

**Author notes:** Ingest Calendar free-busy blocks data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a daily cadence.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "calendar:freebusy", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:freebusy earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Calendar Afternoon Fragmentation** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=calendar:freebusy`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `hour` (>= 13) after dc, sum — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `busy_blocks`, `busy_min`, `hour`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:freebusy
| eval hour=tonumber(strftime(_time,"%H"))
| where hour>=13 AND hour<18
| bin _time span=1d
| stats dc(slot_start) as busy_blocks, sum(busy_min) as busy_min by _time
| where busy_blocks>5 AND busy_min>180
| sort - busy_blocks
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:freebusy earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, busy_blocks, busy_min, hour
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:freebusy earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `hour` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:freebusy earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(hour) AS p50 perc90(hour) AS p90 perc99(hour) AS p99 max(hour) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.13.33: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Daily Afternoon Fragmentation Chart (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `calendar:freebusy` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=calendar:freebusy | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1d` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1d` buckets.
